claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You are inquiring about your 1 child:

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 18 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you about the children you're claiming for:

**How old is the child (or children) you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's name(s)
- Their age(s)

This will help me guide you through the eligibility rules. Child Benefit typically covers children in different ways depending on their age:
- **Under 16**: Generally eligible
- **16-19**: May be eligible if in full-time education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible

Please provide the details of the child/children you're asking about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'm interested in finding out if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is 18, I need to check whether they qualify under the 16-19 category. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to find out about Alex's education or training situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training, or has Alex recently left education?**

To help you answer:
- **In education or training**: This includes full-time school, college, or approved vocational training
- **Left education recently**: If Alex left education within the last 20 weeks, they may still qualify for an extension
- **Neither**: If Alex is neither in education/training nor recently left, they wouldn't qualify

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in full-time education studying for A-levels. That's helpful. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to verify that Alex's education meets the approved criteria for Child Benefit.

**Can you confirm the following about Alex's A-level studies:**

1. **Education type**: A-levels are approved education, which is great! ✓
   
2. **Study hours**: Is Alex studying for at least 12 hours per week under supervision? (This typically covers full-time college A-level students)

3. **Funding**: Is this funded through the college/school, or is it employer-funded training where an employer has arranged or funded the course?

4. **Marital status**: Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?

These details will help me confirm Alex qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I can confirm all of that:

1. Alex is studying A-levels full-time at a local sixth form college
2. Yes, he's there full-time during the week - definitely more than 12 hours of supervised study
3. No, it's not employer-funded - it's just regular college
4. No, Alex isn't married

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Thank you for confirming all of that. Alex meets the approved education criteria perfectly. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great progress! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is in full-time education, this is usually straightforward - but I need to confirm whether Alex has a part-time job and, if so, how many hours per week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is focused entirely on studies with no paid work. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's benefits status:

**Is Alex NOT receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in their own right?**

In other words:
- Is Alex receiving ESA or UC as their own independent claim? (not as a dependent on your claim)
- Or is Alex not receiving these benefits?

Please confirm Alex's benefits situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's still dependent on me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is dependent on you and not receiving any benefits in their own name. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship programme?**

To clarify:
- Since Alex is studying A-levels at college, they're likely not in an apprenticeship
- Just to confirm: Alex is not in any type of apprenticeship scheme (whether in England, Scotland, or Wales)?

Or if Alex is in an apprenticeship, which type and in which country?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - he's just doing A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important part of the eligibility assessment.

**Do any of the following apply to you as the claimant?**

1. **Normally lives in the UK** - You live in the UK as your normal home

2. **Settled status under EU Settlement Scheme** - You have settled status

3. **Pre-settled status and working** - You have pre-settled status AND are working/earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3+ months

4. **Pre-settled status and jobseeking** - You have pre-settled status AND are actively looking for work

5. **Pre-settled status with sufficient resources** - You have pre-settled status AND have enough financial resources to support yourself and family (and NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)

6. **Pre-settled status and studying** - You have pre-settled status AND are studying with sufficient resources

7. **Pre-settled status as family member** - You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside

8. **Crown servant abroad** - You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation? (Usually most UK residents will fall under option 1 - "normally lives in the UK")

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, option 1 applies to me - I normally live in the UK. This is my home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You meet the residency requirements by normally living in the UK. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check whether you're responsible for Alex. Responsibility means one or more of the following:

**Which of these apply to you?**

1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex

2. **Contributing to child's upkeep** - You pay for Alex's care, including things like:
   - Food and clothes
   - Pocket money
   - Housing
   - Presents
   - This can be weekly, monthly, or lump sum payments
   - The amount should be at least equivalent to Child Benefit

3. **Maintenance payments** - You're making maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers Alex's upkeep and equals or exceeds the Child Benefit amount

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which clearly establishes your responsibility for them. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if there are any other claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could anyone else potentially claim for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming or potentially claiming for Alex?
- Could anyone else be claiming for him?

If yes, is this an agreed arrangement between you, or is it disputed?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the sole claimant for Alex. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **In hospital** - Admitted to hospital for treatment
- **In care** - In a care home or local authority care
- **Fostered** - Being looked after by a foster carer
- **Normal living** - Living at home with you (which you mentioned earlier)

Based on what you've already told me, I assume Alex is living at home with you normally - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me normally.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
We're almost at the end of the assessment! One final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- The council is not paying for Alex's housing, food, or other support costs
- You are fully responsible for paying for Alex's upkeep

Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm responsible for everything.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You've provided all the information I need to make a final determination. Let me confirm that Alex meets all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility determination.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

**Great news!** Based on your circumstances, you are **eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

---

### **Why Alex qualifies:**

1. **Age and education status** - Alex is 18 and in full-time approved education (A-levels), which is an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes
2. **Study hours** - Alex meets the requirement of at least 12 hours per week of supervised study
3. **Work status** - Alex is not working, so there's no issue with work hour limits
4. **Benefits** - Alex is not receiving ESA or UC in their own name
5. **Apprenticeship** - Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
6. **Residency** - You normally live in the UK
7. **Responsibility** - You live with Alex and are fully responsible for their upkeep
8. **No other claimant** - You're the sole claimant for Alex
9. **Council support** - The council is not paying towards Alex's care

---

### **Next steps - How to claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide documentation:**
   - Proof of identity for yourself (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Proof of identity for Alex
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
3. **Be aware of High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which reduces or eliminates the benefit
4. **Payment frequency** - Payments are made every 4 weeks on a Monday

---

### **Useful links:**
- [Apply for Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit rates and payments](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/tax-and-other-charges)

If you have any other questions or need further clarification, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is 18 years old and meets all Child Benefit eligibility criteria: (1) Alex is in full-time approved education (A-levels at college) with more than 12 hours per week of supervised study; (2) Alex is not working 24+ hours per week (not in paid work at all); (3) Alex is not receiving ESA or UC in their own name; (4) Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You (the claimant) normally live in the UK; (6) You live with Alex and are responsible for their upkeep; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Alex is living at home normally with you; (9) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility requirements are satisfied.
